content:
For years, collectors have been eagerly seeking memorabilia related to Steve Jobs, and a new auction item seems poised to generate significant interest. It is his eighth-grade science fair project, which comes with two demonstration circuits, along with a note from Jobs to his teacher.

The exhibit has been kept in the Jobs family home in Los Altos since that time, and has now become one of over 200 rare items in an auction celebrating Apple's 50th anniversary...

Celebrating its 50th anniversary this year, Apple has had RR Auctions host a two-part auction in commemoration, titled 'Jobs and the Computer Revolution: Apple 50th Anniversary Auction.' The first part included the first check ever written by Apple, which ultimately sold for as much as $2.4 million.

The second part includes this science fair project.

The note primarily served to remind the teacher that the circuits could burn out if run for too long. As of writing, online bidding had not yet reached $3,000, though the expected price is certain to change.

There is also an early Apple 1 computer that still works properly.

As well as a development prototype of the original iPod.
